sentences.text: Brindabellaspis possesses an elongated ossification that flanks the serial bones supporting the lateral line, a feature similar to maxillary placoderms.
The dorsolaterally positioned eyes of Brindabellaspis suggest it lived a benthic lifestyle.
When discovered in 1980, Brindabellaspis was initially classified as a Weejasperaspid acanthothoracid because of its anatomical similarities to other reef species.
Brindabellaspis was formerly considered part of the orders Acanthothoraci or Rhenanida but was eventually placed in its own order.
Brindabellaspis lived during the Early Devonian period.
The time range for Brindabellaspis is the Emsian stage, spanning from 410.62 to 393.47 million years ago.
